```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
source(file.path("R", "common.R"))
library(knitr)

# The scored summary of all benchmark runs (rescoring of 2026-10-25; every run that finished is in it
# except the release homology runs, see "Data and missing rows"). The file must be in data/benchmark/.
SUMMARY_FILE <- "summary.interim_20261025.tsv"

details <- function(df, summary = "table") {
  knitr::asis_output(paste0("<details><summary>", summary, "</summary>\n\n",
                            paste(knitr::kable(df, format = "html"), collapse = "\n"), "\n\n</details>\n"))
}
```

This notebook supports three parts of the manuscript:

- Methods, benchmark data, compared methods and accuracy measures
  ([`../manuscript/sections/methods_benchmark.tex`](../manuscript/sections/methods_benchmark.tex));
- Results, accuracy across eight eukaryotes, with Table `tab:bench` (Table 1)
  ([`../manuscript/sections/results_benchmark.tex`](../manuscript/sections/results_benchmark.tex));
- Fig. 2 (`fig:benchmark`, `figures/fig2_benchmark.{pdf,png}`), a ggplot2 port of
  `figures/fig2_benchmark/make_fig2.py`.

Provenance: `r evidence("E07")` (benchmark design, inputs, comparator versions and commands),
`r evidence("E25")` (release reruns of TransDecoder and PyTD), `r evidence("E16")` (how the comparator
papers benchmarked; background only, no numbers are taken from it here).

**Which runs.** TransDecoder appears in the benchmark under two sets of labels:

- *earlier final defaults*: `pytd_dev_v2` / `perl_td_dev_v2` (PyTD 48c870c, Perl de3f57e; fixed
  short-ORF test; E07). Earlier drafts of the manuscript quoted these runs; the text, Table 1 and
  Fig. 2 now use the release runs.
- *release*: `pytd_v7` / `perl_td_v7` (PyTD main 3a793ff, Perl devel 41fc5ee; decoy q-value test at
  q 0.05; E25), with the presets `pytd_v7_precise`, `pytd_v7_sensitive` and the homology runs
  `pytd_v7_homology`.

Figures, Table 1 and the numbers written here use the **release** runs (`pytd_v7`). The checks at the
end compare them with the text as it stands, so a mismatch for a TransDecoder number shows a value the
text must update. The section "Release versus earlier final defaults" lists the earlier values next to
the release values. TransDecoder v6.0.0 is an older release that the text compares explicitly, so it is
kept.

```{r data}
S <- read_tab("benchmark", SUMMARY_FILE)
A7 <- read_tab("benchmark", "final_v7", "all_scores.tsv")
IDENT <- read_tab("benchmark", "final_v7", "perl_pytd_identity.tsv")
NEG <- read_tab("benchmark", "final_v7", "negatives_scores.tsv")

TD <- "pytd_v7"; TD_PERL <- "perl_td_v7"; TD_OLD <- "pytd_dev_v2"
INPUTS <- S %>% filter(tool == TD) %>% distinct(org, variant)
N_INPUTS <- nrow(INPUTS)

# value of one metric for one tool and variant, named by organism (in ORGS order; NA if missing)
V <- function(tool, variant, metric) {
  d <- S[S$tool == tool & S$variant == variant, ]
  setNames(d[[metric]][match(ORGS, d$org)], ORGS)
}
MED <- function(tool, variant, metric) median(V(tool, variant, metric), na.rm = TRUE)
r3 <- function(x) round(x, 3)
rng <- function(x) paste0(f3(min(x, na.rm = TRUE)), "-", f3(max(x, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

## Data and missing rows

The notebook reads one scored summary, `data/benchmark/`r SUMMARY_FILE``
(`score_all.py` with the fixed scorer, copied from `$P/work/bench_v3/scores/`; E07, E25). It has
`r num(nrow(S))` rows (tool × input) over `r N_INPUTS` inputs.

```{r missing}
release_and_comparators <- c(TD, TD_PERL, "pytd_v7_precise", "pytd_v7_sensitive", "pytd_v7_homology",
                             "perl_td_v600", "perl_td_v571", "prodigal", "gmst", "codan", "cpat", "cpc2",
                             "rnasamba", "borf", "longest_orf", "angel")
cov <- S %>% filter(tool %in% release_and_comparators) %>% count(tool, name = "rows") %>%
  mutate(tool = factor(tool, levels = release_and_comparators)) %>% arrange(tool)
miss <- function(tool) INPUTS %>% anti_join(S %>% filter(tool == !!tool), by = c("org", "variant"))
codan_miss <- miss("codan")
hom_miss <- miss("pytd_v7_homology")
hom_have <- S %>% filter(tool == "pytd_v7_homology") %>% distinct(org, variant)
hom_a7 <- A7 %>% filter(tool == "pytd_v7_homology") %>% distinct(org, variant)
kable(cov, caption = "Rows per tool (84 inputs in total)")
check_text("CodAn inputs without a row (4 lncRNA + T. thermophila complete.unstranded.wRand)",
           nrow(codan_miss), 5)
check_text("CodAn missing row outside wLnc is only T. thermophila complete.unstranded.wRand (1 = yes)",
           as.numeric(identical(paste(codan_miss$org, codan_miss$variant)[!grepl("wLnc", codan_miss$variant)],
                                "tthermophila complete.unstranded.wRand")), 1)
check_text("pytd_v7_homology rows in all_scores.tsv (all 84 finished)", nrow(hom_a7), 84)
```

Rows missing for the tools used here (all runs have ended; state checked 2026-10-30):

- **CodAn**: `r nrow(codan_miss)` of 84 inputs have no row:
  `r paste(paste(codan_miss$org, codan_miss$variant), collapse = "; ")`.
  The *T. thermophila* `complete.unstranded.wRand` run stopped without output (its files date from
  2026-10-25 03:41, `codan.log` is empty and no CodAn process is running; E07 status update) and was
  not rerun, because CodAn has no ciliate genetic code and its *T. thermophila* runs are not results
  (E27). CodAn has no lncRNA (`wLnc`) runs. None of these inputs is used in Fig. 2 or Table 1, which use the stranded complete,
  complete + random and fragments inputs; CodAn has all 8 organisms there.
- **PyTD with homology** (`pytd_v7_homology`): `r nrow(hom_have)` of 84 rows
  (`r paste(names(table(hom_have$org)), table(hom_have$org), sep = " ", collapse = ", ")`) in this
  summary, which was taken while the runs were in progress. All 84 finished on 2026-10-26 and are scored
  in `final_v7/all_scores.tsv` (`r nrow(hom_a7)` rows; E25); the section on homology below uses those.
  These runs are not in Fig. 2 or Table 1. The manuscript's homology results use the released homology
  mode (`pytd_v7h_homology`, PyTD a5b24c3, with homology-assisted start refinement; notebook 05,
  Fig. 5d,e; E25 addendum 2026-10-28).
- `--precise` and `--sensitive` were run on the negative-containing inputs only (20 each; E25).
- RNAsamba was run on stranded inputs only (44); v6.0.0, v5.7.1 and the longest-ORF baseline have no
  lncRNA inputs (80); ANGEL has 3 runs (dropped, Methods).

### Agreement with the release score table (E25)

`data/benchmark/final_v7/all_scores.tsv` was scored with `score_v7.sh` from the same runs (E25).

```{r a7-consistency}
key <- c("org", "variant", "tool")
metric_cols <- setdiff(names(A7), key)
J <- inner_join(S, A7, by = key, suffix = c(".s", ".a"))
diffs <- bind_rows(lapply(metric_cols, function(m) {
  d <- abs(J[[paste0(m, ".s")]] - J[[paste0(m, ".a")]]) > 1e-9
  tibble(column = m, rows_compared = nrow(J), rows_differing = sum(d, na.rm = TRUE))
}))
cons <- J %>% count(tool, name = "rows_in_both")
n_diff_cells <- sum(diffs$rows_differing)
kable(cons)
details(diffs, "differences per column")
```

All `r nrow(J)` rows of `all_scores.tsv` (`pytd_v7`, `perl_td_v7`, `pytd_dev_v2`, `perl_td_dev_v2`;
84 each) are in the summary, and `r n_diff_cells` cells differ, including run times. The two tables
agree for `pytd_v7`.

### Genetic-code compatibility

*T. thermophila* reads TAA and TAG as glutamine. GeneMarkS-T (tables 1, 4 and 11 only), CodAn, CPC2,
RNAsamba and Borf have no option for this code; they were run with the standard code, so their
*T. thermophila* results show only that the code is unsupported. These tool × organism results are
**excluded** from everything below (reported as not applicable): Fig. 2 marks them "n/a", their
Table 1 medians are over the other seven organisms, and the rankings leave out *T. thermophila*. Their
values are listed here and kept in `S_raw` (also used for run times, which do not depend on the code).
TransDecoder (`-G Tetrahymena`), Prodigal (`-g 6`) and CPAT (TGA as the only stop) were run with the
ciliate code.

```{r code-compat}
INCOMPATIBLE <- c("gmst", "codan", "cpc2", "rnasamba", "borf")
S_raw <- S
S <- S %>% filter(!(org == "tthermophila" & tool %in% INCOMPATIBLE))
details(S_raw %>% filter(org == "tthermophila", tool %in% INCOMPATIBLE,
                         variant %in% c("complete", "fragments", "complete.wRand")) %>%
          select(tool, variant, f1_stop, f1_exact, precision_stop) %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), r3)),
        "excluded: standard-code tools on T. thermophila (stranded inputs)")
```

## Benchmark data (Methods)

```{r methods-data}
GENES_TEX <- c(human = 19167, mouse = 21409, dmel = 13884, athal = 26867, spombe = 5100,
               tthermophila = 26456, pfalciparum = 5281, creinhardtii = 17621)
genes <- S %>% filter(tool == TD, variant == "complete") %>% select(org, n_truth)
genes <- genes[match(ORGS, genes$org), ] %>% mutate(organism = ORG_LABEL[org], manuscript = GENES_TEX[org])
per_org <- INPUTS %>% filter(!grepl("wLnc", variant)) %>% count(org)
lnc_inputs <- INPUTS %>% filter(grepl("wLnc", variant))
n_lnc <- NEG %>% filter(variant == "complete.wLnc", label == TD) %>% select(org, n_neg)
n_lnc <- setNames(n_lnc$n_neg, n_lnc$org)
stopifnot(all(S$n_truth[S$tool == TD] == genes$n_truth[match(S$org[S$tool == TD], genes$org)]))
kable(genes %>% select(organism, genes = n_truth, manuscript), caption = "Truth-set genes (complete input)")
```

- Eight organisms; truth-set sizes from `r num(min(genes$n_truth))` (*S. pombe*) to
  `r num(max(genes$n_truth))` (*A. thaliana*) genes. Every input of an organism has the same
  `n_truth`.
- `r unique(per_org$n)` inputs per organism without lncRNA negatives, plus `r nrow(lnc_inputs)` lncRNA
  inputs (human and mouse, complete and fragments): `r N_INPUTS` inputs in total.
- lncRNA negatives: `r num(n_lnc[["human"]])` (human) and `r num(n_lnc[["mouse"]])` (mouse)
  (`negatives_scores.tsv`, E25).
- The G+C values of Table `tab:orgs` and the numbers of UTRs added (0 to 1,142) come from the truth
  logs and input FASTAs (E07) and are not in a committed table; they are not recomputed here.

## Compared methods (Methods)

```{r methods-tools}
v6 <- S %>% filter(tool %in% c("perl_td_v600", "perl_td_v571")) %>%
  select(org, variant, tool, all_of(setdiff(metric_cols, "runtime_sec"))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(org, variant, tool)) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = tool) %>% filter(!is.na(perl_td_v600))
v6_inputs <- n_distinct(paste(v6$org, v6$variant))
v6_same <- v6 %>% group_by(org, variant) %>% summarise(same = all(perl_td_v600 == perl_td_v571), .groups = "drop")
angel <- S %>% filter(tool == "angel") %>% transmute(org, variant, hours = runtime_sec / 3600)
others_athal <- S %>% filter(org == "athal", variant == "complete",
                             tool %in% c(TD, TD_PERL, "prodigal", "gmst", "cpat", "cpc2", "rnasamba", "borf", "codan")) %>%
  transmute(tool, minutes = round(runtime_sec / 60, 1)) %>% arrange(minutes)
kable(angel %>% mutate(hours = round(hours, 1)), caption = "ANGEL runs")
kable(others_athal, caption = "Other tools, A. thaliana complete")
```

- v5.7.1 and v6.0.0 have identical scores on all `r sum(v6_same$same)` of `r v6_inputs` inputs they
  share (every score column). E07 checked that their `preds.tsv` files are byte-identical.
- ANGEL: `r nrow(angel)` *A. thaliana* runs of `r f1(min(angel$hours))`-`r f1(max(angel$hours))` h
  (wall clock). On the *A. thaliana* complete input, all other tools except CodAn
  (`r f1(others_athal$minutes[others_athal$tool == "codan"] / 60)` h) took
  `r f1(min(others_athal$minutes))`-`r f1(max(others_athal$minutes[others_athal$tool != "codan"]))` min.

## Accuracy measures (Methods)

The scoring rules (stop within 2 nt; exact within 2 nt at both ends) are applied by `score_predictions.py`
(E07). Runtimes are wall-clock seconds per run (`runtime_sec`) under 6-16 concurrent jobs on a shared
28-core host (E07); the concurrency is from the launch logs, not from a table here.

## Table 1: benchmark accuracy

Median over the eight organisms, stranded inputs: stop and exact F1 on complete and fragments, and
stop-level precision on complete + random (`complete.wRand`). For the tools that do not support the ciliate code,
the medians are over the other seven organisms (*T. thermophila* not applicable).

```{r table1}
TOOLS <- c(pytd_v7 = "TransDecoder (release)", perl_td_v600 = "TransDecoder v6.0.0",
           longest_orf = "longest ORF", prodigal = "Prodigal", gmst = "GeneMarkS-T", cpat = "CPAT",
           rnasamba = "RNAsamba", cpc2 = "CPC2", borf = "Borf", codan = "CodAn")
COLS <- tribble(~col, ~variant, ~metric,
                "complete_stop_f1", "complete", "f1_stop",
                "complete_exact_f1", "complete", "f1_exact",
                "fragments_stop_f1", "fragments", "f1_stop",
                "fragments_exact_f1", "fragments", "f1_exact",
                "complete_rand_precision", "complete.wRand", "precision_stop")
tab1_long <- tidyr::crossing(tool = names(TOOLS), COLS) %>% rowwise() %>%
  mutate(median = MED(tool, variant, metric), n_orgs = sum(!is.na(V(tool, variant, metric)))) %>% ungroup()
table1 <- tab1_long %>% select(tool, col, median) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = median) %>%
  left_join(tab1_long %>% group_by(tool) %>% summarise(min_orgs = min(n_orgs)), by = "tool") %>%
  mutate(label = TOOLS[tool], tool = factor(tool, levels = names(TOOLS))) %>% arrange(tool) %>%
  mutate(tool = as.character(tool),
         note = case_when(tool %in% INCOMPATIBLE ~ "7 organisms (ciliate code not supported)",
                          min_orgs < 8 ~ sprintf("interim: %d of 8 organisms in some column", min_orgs),
                          TRUE ~ "")) %>%
  select(tool, label, all_of(COLS$col), min_orgs, note)
write_tsv(table1 %>% mutate(across(all_of(COLS$col), ~ round(.x, 4))),
          data_path("benchmark", "final_v7", "table1.tsv"))
T1 <- function(tool, col) table1[[col]][table1$tool == tool]
kableExtra::kable_styling(kable(table1 %>% select(-tool, -min_orgs) %>% mutate(across(all_of(COLS$col), r3)),
  col.names = c("method", "complete stop F1", "complete exact F1", "fragments stop F1", "fragments exact F1",
                "complete + rand precision", "note"),
  caption = sprintf("Table 1 (from %s; written to data/benchmark/final_v7/table1.tsv)", SUMMARY_FILE)),
  full_width = FALSE)
```

`r if (all(table1$min_orgs[!table1$tool %in% INCOMPATIBLE] == 8)) "All other cells are medians over all 8 organisms." else "Rows marked interim are medians over the available organisms."`
The manuscript row for CodAn is still a placeholder; the computed CodAn row is
`r paste(f3(unlist(table1[table1$tool == "codan", COLS$col])), collapse = " / ")`.

## Fig. 2: accuracy on eight eukaryotes

Stranded inputs, organisms ordered by transcriptome G+C. Panels a-e are heatmaps (colour clipped at
0.4); panel f is the run time on complete inputs, median and range over organisms. Cells marked "n/a"
are tools that do not support the ciliate code on *T. thermophila* (GeneMarkS-T, CodAn, CPC2,
RNAsamba, Borf; not applicable, above); grey cells marked "pend." are rows missing from the summary. TransDecoder is the release default
(`pytd_v7`, identical to `perl_td_v7`).

```{r fig2-data}
HEAT_TOOLS <- c(pytd_v7 = "TransDecoder", perl_td_v600 = "TransDecoder v6.0.0", prodigal = "Prodigal",
                gmst = "GeneMarkS-T", codan = "CodAn", cpat = "CPAT", cpc2 = "CPC2", rnasamba = "RNAsamba",
                borf = "Borf", longest_orf = "longest ORF")
WRONG_CODE <- c("gmst", "codan", "cpc2", "rnasamba", "borf")
PANELS <- tribble(~panel, ~variant, ~metric, ~title,
                  "a", "complete", "f1_stop", "complete: stop-level F1",
                  "b", "complete", "f1_exact", "complete: exact F1",
                  "c", "complete.wRand", "precision_stop", "complete + random: precision",
                  "d", "fragments", "f1_stop", "fragments: stop-level F1",
                  "e", "fragments", "f1_exact", "fragments: exact F1")
ORG_SHORT <- c(pfalciparum = "P. fal.", tthermophila = "T. the.", spombe = "S. pom.", athal = "A. tha.",
               dmel = "D. mel.", mouse = "M. mus.", human = "H. sap.", creinhardtii = "C. rei.")
heat <- tidyr::crossing(PANELS, tool = names(HEAT_TOOLS), org = ORGS) %>% rowwise() %>%
  mutate(value = V(tool, variant, metric)[[org]]) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(wrong = org == "tthermophila" & tool %in% WRONG_CODE,
         x = match(org, ORGS), y = length(HEAT_TOOLS) + 1 - match(tool, names(HEAT_TOOLS)),
         lab = ifelse(wrong, "n/a", ifelse(is.na(value), "pend.", ifelse(round(value, 2) >= 1, "1.0", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.2f", value))))))
n_pending <- sum(is.na(heat$value) & !heat$wrong)

RT_TOOLS <- c(pytd_v7 = "PyTD", perl_td_v7 = "TD (Perl)", prodigal = "Prodigal",
              gmst = "GeneMarkS-T", codan = "CodAn", cpat = "CPAT", cpc2 = "CPC2", rnasamba = "RNAsamba",
              borf = "Borf", angel = "ANGEL")
rt <- S_raw %>% filter(variant == "complete", tool %in% names(RT_TOOLS)) %>% group_by(tool) %>%
  summarise(median = median(runtime_sec), min = min(runtime_sec), max = max(runtime_sec), n = n()) %>%
  mutate(label = RT_TOOLS[tool], y = length(RT_TOOLS) + 1 - match(tool, names(RT_TOOLS)),
         note = case_when(tool == "angel" ~ sprintf("%.0f h (A. thal.)", median / 3600),
                          median > 3600 ~ sprintf("%.1f h%s", median / 3600, ifelse(n == 8, "", sprintf("  (n = %d)", n))),
                          TRUE ~ paste0(num(round(median)), " s", ifelse(n == 8, "", sprintf("  (n = %d)", n)))))
```

```{r fig2, fig.width = FULL_W, fig.height = 128 * MM}
heat_fill <- scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#f7fbff", "#c6dbef", "#6baed6", "#2171b5", "#08306b"),
                                  limits = c(0.4, 1), oob = scales::squish, breaks = c(0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1),
                                  labels = c("≤0.4", "0.6", "0.8", "1.0"), name = "F1 or precision",
                                  na.value = "#dddddd")
hatch <- function(d) {   # diagonal lines inside each hatched cell
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(NULL)
  offs <- seq(-0.8, 0.8, by = 0.2)
  segs <- tidyr::crossing(d %>% select(x, y), o = offs) %>%
    mutate(x0 = pmax(-0.5, -0.5 + o), y0 = pmax(-0.5, -0.5 - o), x1 = pmin(0.5, 0.5 + o), y1 = pmin(0.5, 0.5 - o)) %>%
    filter(x1 > x0)
  geom_segment(data = segs, aes(x = x + x0, y = y + y0, xend = x + x1, yend = y + y1),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "#aaaaaa", linewidth = 0.15)
}
heat_panel <- function(p, show_rows) {
  d <- heat %>% filter(panel == p)
  ok <- d %>% filter(!wrong)
  ggplot(ok, aes(x, y)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = value), colour = NA) +
    geom_tile(data = d %>% filter(wrong), fill = "#f2f2f2", colour = NA) +
    geom_text(aes(label = lab, colour = !is.na(value) & (pmin(value, 1) - 0.4) / 0.6 > 0.55), size = 1.62) +
    geom_text(data = d %>% filter(wrong), aes(label = lab), colour = "#888888", size = 1.5) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "#222222"), guide = "none") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = length(HEAT_TOOLS) + 0.5 - c(2, 5, 9), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
    heat_fill +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(ORGS), labels = ORG_SHORT[ORGS], expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq_along(HEAT_TOOLS), labels = if (show_rows) rev(HEAT_TOOLS) else NULL,
                       expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = PANELS$title[PANELS$panel == p]) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 55, hjust = 1, face = "italic", size = 5.6),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6), axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank())
}
rt_panel <- ggplot(rt, aes(y = y)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = min, xend = max, yend = y, colour = tool %in% c(TD, TD_PERL)), linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(aes(x = median, colour = tool %in% c(TD, TD_PERL)), size = 1.2) +
  geom_text(aes(x = pmax(max, median) * 1.35, label = note), hjust = 0, size = 1.9, colour = "#444444") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = TD_C, `FALSE` = "#6b6b6b"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_log10(limits = c(5, 3e7), breaks = c(10, 1e3, 1e5), labels = c("10 s", expression(10^3~s), expression(10^5~s))) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = rt$y, labels = rt$label) +
  labs(x = "wall-clock time (log scale)", y = NULL,
       title = "run time, complete inputs") +
  theme(axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6))
fig2 <- (heat_panel("a", TRUE) + heat_panel("b", FALSE) + heat_panel("c", FALSE) +
         heat_panel("d", TRUE) + heat_panel("e", FALSE) + rt_panel) +
  plot_layout(ncol = 3, guides = "collect") + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(8, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(2.5, "mm"),
        legend.title.position = "top")
png_f <- save_fig(fig2, "fig2_benchmark", FULL_W, 128 * MM)
fig2
```

Pending cells in the heatmaps: `r n_pending`. Not-applicable cells: `r sum(heat$wrong) / nrow(PANELS)` per panel.

```{r fig2-tables, results = "asis"}
for (p in PANELS$panel) {
  w <- heat %>% filter(panel == p) %>% arrange(match(tool, names(HEAT_TOOLS)), match(org, ORGS)) %>%
    transmute(method = HEAT_TOOLS[tool], org = ORG_LABEL[org], value = r3(value)) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = org, values_from = value)
  print(details(w, sprintf("panel %s: %s (values)", p, PANELS$title[PANELS$panel == p])))
}
print(details(rt %>% arrange(desc(y)) %>% transmute(method = label, n, median_s = round(median, 1),
                                                     min_s = round(min, 1), max_s = round(max, 1)),
              "panel f: run time on complete inputs (seconds)"))
```

## Implementations: Perl and Python

```{r concordance}
n_ident <- sum(IDENT$identical)
pp <- S %>% filter(tool %in% c(TD, TD_PERL)) %>% select(org, variant, tool, all_of(setdiff(metric_cols, "runtime_sec"))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(org, variant, tool)) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = tool)
n_score_diff <- sum(pp[[TD]] != pp[[TD_PERL]])
ratio <- S %>% filter(tool %in% c(TD, TD_PERL)) %>% select(org, variant, tool, runtime_sec) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = tool, values_from = runtime_sec) %>% mutate(ratio = .data[[TD_PERL]] / .data[[TD]])
ratio_c <- ratio %>% filter(variant == "complete")
rt_med <- function(tool) median(S$runtime_sec[S$tool == tool & S$variant == "complete"])
ident_rt <- IDENT %>% inner_join(ratio, by = c("org", "variant"))
stopifnot(all(abs(ident_rt$perl_runtime_sec - ident_rt[[TD_PERL]]) < 1e-6),
          all(abs(ident_rt$pytd_runtime_sec - ident_rt[[TD]]) < 1e-6))
```

- Predictions of the Perl and Python release versions are identical in `r n_ident` of `r nrow(IDENT)`
  inputs (`perl_pytd_identity.tsv`: sorted `preds.tsv` compared, E25), and all score columns agree
  (`r n_score_diff` differing cells). One set of numbers describes both implementations.
- Run time, Perl / Python: median ratio `r sprintf("%.2f", median(ratio$ratio))`
  (`r sprintf("%.2f", min(ratio$ratio))`-`r sprintf("%.2f", max(ratio$ratio))`) over the 84 inputs;
  on complete inputs `r sprintf("%.2f", median(ratio_c$ratio))`. Median run time on complete inputs:
  Python `r num(round(rt_med(TD)))` s, Perl `r num(round(rt_med(TD_PERL)))` s (earlier final defaults:
  `r num(round(rt_med(TD_OLD)))` s and `r num(round(rt_med("perl_td_dev_v2")))` s). Shared host,
  indicative only. The 2.3-fold figure in the abstract and in Results, algorithm, is for the earlier
  runs and is checked in `01_algorithm.Rmd`.

## Accuracy across eight eukaryotes

The text opens by stating that the Perl and Python implementations gave identical predictions; see
the section above (`r n_ident`/84 inputs, release versions). `r evidence("E25")`

### Stop codons

```{r stop}
td_cs <- V(TD, "complete", "f1_stop"); v6_cs <- V("perl_td_v600", "complete", "f1_stop")
lo_cs <- V("longest_orf", "complete", "f1_stop")
td_v6_maxdiff <- max(abs(td_cs - v6_cs))
```

On complete transcripts, the release default had a stop-level F1 of `r rng(td_cs)` (median
`r f3(median(td_cs))`), against `r rng(v6_cs)` for v6.0.0 and `r rng(lo_cs)` for the longest-ORF
baseline. Per organism, the release default was within `r f3(td_v6_maxdiff)` of v6.0.0 at the stop
level. `r evidence("E07")`, `r evidence("E25")`

### Noncoding sequence

```{r noncoding}
td_p <- V(TD, "complete.wRand", "precision_stop")
pr_p <- V("prodigal", "complete.wRand", "precision_stop")
lo_p <- V("longest_orf", "complete.wRand", "precision_stop")
cp_p <- V("cpat", "complete.wRand", "precision_stop")
```

With one GC-matched random sequence per transcript, the release default kept a median stop-level
precision of `r f3(median(td_p))` (`r rng(td_p)`), and its median stop F1 went from
`r f3(median(td_cs))` to `r f3(MED(TD, "complete.wRand", "f1_stop"))`. Prodigal's precision was
`r rng(pr_p)` (median `r f3(median(pr_p))`), and its median stop F1 went from
`r f3(MED("prodigal", "complete", "f1_stop"))` to `r f3(MED("prodigal", "complete.wRand", "f1_stop"))`.
The longest-ORF baseline had a median precision of `r f3(median(lo_p))` (*C. reinhardtii*
`r f3(lo_p[["creinhardtii"]])`). RNAsamba `r f3(MED("rnasamba", "complete.wRand", "precision_stop"))`,
Borf `r f3(MED("borf", "complete.wRand", "precision_stop"))`; CPAT `r f3(median(cp_p))`
(*C. reinhardtii* `r f3(cp_p[["creinhardtii"]])`).

### Start codons

```{r starts}
td_ce <- V(TD, "complete", "f1_exact"); v6_ce <- V("perl_td_v600", "complete", "f1_exact")
cls_ce <- sapply(c("cpat", "rnasamba", "cpc2"), MED, variant = "complete", metric = "f1_exact")
cls_fe <- sapply(c("cpat", "rnasamba", "cpc2"), MED, variant = "fragments", metric = "f1_exact")
```

The longest-ORF baseline had a median exact F1 of `r f3(MED("longest_orf", "complete", "f1_exact"))`.
The release default had an exact F1 of `r rng(td_ce)` on complete transcripts (median
`r f3(median(td_ce))`), against `r rng(v6_ce)` (median `r f3(median(v6_ce))`) for v6.0.0. Prodigal
median `r f3(MED("prodigal", "complete", "f1_exact"))`, GeneMarkS-T
`r f3(MED("gmst", "complete", "f1_exact"))`. CPAT, RNAsamba and CPC2: medians `r rng(cls_ce)` on
complete transcripts and `r rng(cls_fe)` on fragments (TransDecoder `r f3(MED(TD, "fragments", "f1_exact"))`).

### Fragments

```{r fragments}
td_fs <- V(TD, "fragments", "f1_stop"); pr_fs <- V("prodigal", "fragments", "f1_stop")
td_fe <- V(TD, "fragments", "f1_exact"); pr_fe <- V("prodigal", "fragments", "f1_exact")
prod_better_stop <- names(which(pr_fs > td_fs))
td_better_exact <- names(which(td_fe > pr_fe))
kable(tibble(organism = ORG_LABEL[ORGS], TD_stop = r3(td_fs), Prodigal_stop = r3(pr_fs),
             TD_exact = r3(td_fe), Prodigal_exact = r3(pr_fe)))
```

On fragments, Prodigal had the higher stop F1 in `r length(prod_better_stop)` of 8 organisms (median
`r f3(median(pr_fs))` vs `r f3(median(td_fs))`); *T. thermophila*: `r f3(pr_fs[["tthermophila"]])` vs
`r f3(td_fs[["tthermophila"]])`. At the exact level TransDecoder was higher in
`r paste(ORG_LABEL[td_better_exact], collapse = ", ")`.

### Ciliate genetic code

```{r ciliate}
std_tools <- c("gmst", "rnasamba", "cpc2", "borf")
tthe_std <- S_raw %>% filter(org == "tthermophila", tool %in% std_tools, variant %in% c("complete", "fragments")) %>%
  select(tool, variant, f1_stop, f1_exact)
tthe_max <- max(c(tthe_std$f1_stop, tthe_std$f1_exact))
codan_tthe <- S_raw %>% filter(org == "tthermophila", tool == "codan", variant %in% c("complete", "fragments", "complete.wRand")) %>%
  select(variant, f1_stop, f1_exact, precision_stop)
TT <- function(tool, variant, metric) V(tool, variant, metric)[["tthermophila"]]
kable(tthe_std)
kable(codan_tthe, caption = "CodAn on T. thermophila (standard code)")
```

Run with the standard code, GeneMarkS-T, RNAsamba, CPC2 and Borf had F1 of at most
`r f3(tthe_max)` on *T. thermophila* (stranded complete and fragments). CodAn, also with the standard
code: stop F1 `r f3(TT("codan", "complete", "f1_stop"))` (complete) and
`r f3(TT("codan", "fragments", "f1_stop"))` (fragments). With the ciliate code, the release default
reached a stop F1 of `r f3(TT(TD, "complete", "f1_stop"))` and an exact F1 of
`r f3(TT(TD, "complete", "f1_exact"))` on complete transcripts; v6.0.0
`r f3(TT("perl_td_v600", "complete", "f1_stop"))` / `r f3(TT("perl_td_v600", "complete", "f1_exact"))`,
Prodigal `r f3(TT("prodigal", "complete", "f1_stop"))` / `r f3(TT("prodigal", "complete", "f1_exact"))`,
CPAT `r f3(TT("cpat", "complete", "f1_stop"))` / `r f3(TT("cpat", "complete", "f1_exact"))`. Precision
with random sequences: `r f3(TT(TD, "complete.wRand", "precision_stop"))` (release default),
`r f3(TT("perl_td_v600", "complete.wRand", "precision_stop"))` (v6.0.0),
`r f3(TT("prodigal", "complete.wRand", "precision_stop"))` (Prodigal).

### GC extremes

```{r gc}
cre_others <- sapply(c("perl_td_v600", "prodigal", "gmst", "cpat"), function(t) V(t, "complete", "f1_exact")[["creinhardtii"]])
```

*P. falciparum*: exact F1 `r f3(td_ce[["pfalciparum"]])` (highest of the eight:
`r ORG_LABEL[names(which.max(td_ce))]`), stop F1 `r f3(td_cs[["pfalciparum"]])`. *C. reinhardtii*:
stop F1 `r f3(td_cs[["creinhardtii"]])`, exact F1 `r f3(td_ce[["creinhardtii"]])` (lowest:
`r ORG_LABEL[names(which.min(td_ce))]`). Other methods on *C. reinhardtii* (v6.0.0, Prodigal,
GeneMarkS-T, CPAT): exact F1 `r rng(cre_others)`.

## Homology evidence

The Methods list PyTD with DIAMOND/Pfam evidence. Release homology runs (`pytd_v7_homology`, PyTD
3a793ff, before the homology-assisted start refinement): all `r nrow(hom_a7)` of 84, from `final_v7/all_scores.tsv` (E25). The
manuscript's homology numbers on the benchmark inputs come from the released homology mode
(`pytd_v7h_homology`, which also uses homology in start refinement) and are reproduced in notebook 05.

```{r homology}
hom <- A7 %>% filter(tool %in% c(TD, "pytd_v7_homology")) %>%
  select(org, variant, tool, sensitivity_stop, precision_stop, f1_exact) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = tool, values_from = c(sensitivity_stop, precision_stop, f1_exact)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(sensitivity_stop_pytd_v7_homology)) %>%
  transmute(org, variant, d_sens_stop = sensitivity_stop_pytd_v7_homology - sensitivity_stop_pytd_v7,
            d_prec_stop = precision_stop_pytd_v7_homology - precision_stop_pytd_v7,
            d_f1_exact = f1_exact_pytd_v7_homology - f1_exact_pytd_v7,
            type = ifelse(grepl("^fragments", variant), "fragments", "complete-type"))
hom_sum <- hom %>% group_by(type) %>% summarise(inputs = n(), across(starts_with("d_"), list(min = min, max = max)))
kable(hom_sum %>% mutate(across(starts_with("d_"), ~ round(.x, 4))),
      caption = "Homology (pytd_v7_homology, 3a793ff) minus ab initio (release), 84 inputs")
details(hom %>% mutate(across(starts_with("d_"), ~ round(.x, 4))), "per input")
```

## Fragments by partial type

Each fragment keeps either the 3' piece of the transcript (stop present, start lost: a 5' partial
CDS) or the 5' piece (start present, stop lost: a 3' partial CDS), about half each. For a 3' partial
the reference 3' end is the last whole codon at the fragment end, so a stop-level match means the
prediction runs to the fragment end; for a 5' partial an exact match means it starts at the fragment
start (no start codon). Table from `pipeline/derive/02_partial_types.py` (same matching as
`score_predictions.py`; summed over the two types it reproduces every true-positive count of the
summary). Stranded fragments, median over organisms (seven for the tools that do not support the
ciliate code). Precision is over predictions on fragments of that type.
Fragments with both ends missing (internal) are scored in the balanced mixed inputs (next section).

```{r partial-types}
PT <- read_tab("benchmark", "final_v7", "partial_types.tsv") %>%
  filter(!(org == "tthermophila" & tool %in% INCOMPATIBLE))
PT_TOOLS <- c(pytd_v7 = "TransDecoder", perl_td_v600 = "TransDecoder v6.0.0", prodigal = "Prodigal",
              gmst = "GeneMarkS-T", codan = "CodAn", cpat = "CPAT", cpc2 = "CPC2", rnasamba = "RNAsamba",
              borf = "Borf", longest_orf = "longest ORF")
pt <- PT %>% filter(variant == "fragments", tool %in% names(PT_TOOLS)) %>%
  mutate(type = recode(type, `5prime_partial` = "5' partial (start lost)", `3prime_partial` = "3' partial (stop lost)")) %>%
  group_by(tool, type) %>%
  summarise(n_org = n(), across(c(sensitivity_stop, sensitivity_exact, precision_stop), median), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(method = factor(PT_TOOLS[tool], levels = PT_TOOLS)) %>% arrange(method, type)
pt_wide <- pt %>% select(method, type, sensitivity_stop, sensitivity_exact, precision_stop) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = c(sensitivity_stop, sensitivity_exact, precision_stop), names_glue = "{type}: {.value}")
kable(pt_wide %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), r3)))
details(PT %>% filter(tool %in% names(PT_TOOLS)) %>% mutate(across(starts_with(c("sens", "prec")), r3)),
        "per organism, input and tool")
PTV <- function(tool, type, m) pt[[m]][pt$tool == tool & grepl(paste0("^", type), pt$type)]
```

TransDecoder: on 3' partials stop-level sensitivity `r f3(PTV(TD, "3'", "sensitivity_stop"))`, exact
`r f3(PTV(TD, "3'", "sensitivity_exact"))`; on 5' partials `r f3(PTV(TD, "5'", "sensitivity_stop"))`
and `r f3(PTV(TD, "5'", "sensitivity_exact"))`. Prodigal: 3' partials `r f3(PTV("prodigal", "3'", "sensitivity_stop"))` /
`r f3(PTV("prodigal", "3'", "sensitivity_exact"))`, 5' partials `r f3(PTV("prodigal", "5'", "sensitivity_stop"))` /
`r f3(PTV("prodigal", "5'", "sensitivity_exact"))`. The classifiers that require an ATG (CPAT, CPC2,
RNAsamba) have exact sensitivity of at most `r f3(max(sapply(c("cpat", "cpc2", "rnasamba"), PTV, type = "5'", m = "sensitivity_exact")))`
on 5' partials.

## Balanced mixed inputs

The `fragments` inputs hold one partial type per sequence and no complete transcripts, and have no
internal fragments (both ends missing). Methods that train on their input (TransDecoder's coding and
start models, GeneMarkS-T, Prodigal) are affected by such a composition. The balanced mixed inputs
`fragments_mixed_t1`, `_t2` and `_t3` (`pipeline/benchmark/make_mixed_inputs.py`, `r evidence("E28")`)
are built from the same transcripts as `fragments` (UTRs at most 250 nt). Each one assigns every transcript at random to one of four
equal groups:

- complete (unchanged);
- 5' partial: cut inside codons 2 to 80% of the CDS, uniformly, keeping the 3' piece;
- 3' partial: cut from 20% of the CDS to just before the stop codon, uniformly, keeping the 5' piece;
- internal: a window of about half the CDS (fraction from $\mathcal N(0.5,0.1)$), with both ends inside the CDS.

At least 150 nt of CDS must remain. Trials 1-3 use seeds 1-3 for both the assignment and the
cuts. The inputs are stranded, the tools were run as for `fragments` (CodAn partial models,
RNAsamba partial weights) and the scoring is the same. For an internal fragment, a stop-level match
means the prediction runs to the fragment end; an exact match means it also starts at the fragment start.
Values are the median over organisms (seven for the tools without the ciliate code) in each trial,
shown as the mean over the three trials (min-max over trials). The longest-ORF baseline is the
longest ORF of the `pytd_v7` LongOrfs run.

```{r mixed}
MX_TOOLS <- c(pytd_v7 = "TransDecoder", perl_td_v600 = "TransDecoder v6.0.0", longest_orf = "longest ORF",
              prodigal = "Prodigal", gmst = "GeneMarkS-T", codan = "CodAn", cpat = "CPAT", rnasamba = "RNAsamba",
              cpc2 = "CPC2", borf = "Borf")
trial_of <- function(v) sub("fragments_mixed_", "", v)
MX_RAW <- read_tab("benchmark", "final_v7", "mixed_scores.tsv") %>% mutate(trial = trial_of(variant))
MX <- MX_RAW %>% filter(!(org == "tthermophila" & tool %in% INCOMPATIBLE))
mr <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f (%.3f-%.3f)", mean(x), min(x), max(x))
mx_metrics <- c("sensitivity_stop", "precision_stop", "f1_stop", "sensitivity_exact", "precision_exact", "f1_exact")
mx_trial <- MX %>% filter(tool %in% names(MX_TOOLS)) %>% group_by(tool, trial) %>%
  summarise(n_org = n(), across(all_of(mx_metrics), median), .groups = "drop")
mx <- mx_trial %>% group_by(tool) %>%
  summarise(organisms = paste(unique(range(n_org)), collapse = "-"), trials = n(),
            across(all_of(mx_metrics), mr), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(method = factor(MX_TOOLS[tool], levels = MX_TOOLS)) %>% arrange(method) %>%
  select(method, organisms, trials, all_of(mx_metrics))
mx_mean <- mx_trial %>% group_by(tool) %>% summarise(across(all_of(mx_metrics), mean), .groups = "drop")
MXV <- function(tool, m) mx_mean[[m]][mx_mean$tool == tool]
mx_n <- MX %>% filter(tool == TD) %>% select(org, trial, n_truth) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = trial, values_from = n_truth)
mx_trial_spread <- mx_trial %>% group_by(tool) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(mx_metrics), ~ max(.x) - min(.x)), .groups = "drop")
kable(mx, caption = "Balanced mixed inputs: all references, median over organisms, mean (range) over 3 trials")
details(mx_n %>% mutate(organism = ORG_LABEL[org]) %>% select(organism, starts_with("t")),
        "references per organism and trial")
details(MX %>% filter(tool %in% names(MX_TOOLS)) %>%
          select(org, trial, tool, n_truth, n_pred, tp_stop, tp_exact, all_of(mx_metrics), runtime_sec) %>%
          mutate(across(all_of(mx_metrics), r3), runtime_sec = round(runtime_sec)) %>% arrange(org, tool, trial),
        "per organism, trial and tool")
```

Over the three trials the per-trial medians of every method and measure vary by at most
`r f3(max(as.matrix(mx_trial_spread[, mx_metrics])))` (largest range). TransDecoder: stop-level F1
`r f3(MXV(TD, "f1_stop"))`, exact F1 `r f3(MXV(TD, "f1_exact"))`; Prodigal `r f3(MXV("prodigal", "f1_stop"))` /
`r f3(MXV("prodigal", "f1_exact"))`; GeneMarkS-T `r f3(MXV("gmst", "f1_stop"))` / `r f3(MXV("gmst", "f1_exact"))`;
longest ORF `r f3(MXV("longest_orf", "f1_stop"))` / `r f3(MXV("longest_orf", "f1_exact"))`.

**By partial type** (`02_partial_types.py` on the mixed inputs). Sensitivity is per type. Precision
is over the predictions on sequences of that type, as in the previous section.

```{r mixed-types}
MPT <- read_tab("benchmark", "final_v7", "partial_types.tsv") %>%
  filter(grepl("^fragments_mixed_", variant), !(org == "tthermophila" & tool %in% INCOMPATIBLE),
         tool %in% names(MX_TOOLS)) %>% mutate(trial = trial_of(variant))
TYPE_LABEL <- c(complete = "complete", `5prime_partial` = "5' partial", `3prime_partial` = "3' partial",
                internal = "internal")
mpt_trial <- MPT %>% group_by(tool, type, trial) %>%
  summarise(across(c(sensitivity_stop, sensitivity_exact, precision_stop), median), .groups = "drop")
mpt_mean <- mpt_trial %>% group_by(tool, type) %>%
  summarise(across(c(sensitivity_stop, sensitivity_exact, precision_stop), mean), .groups = "drop")
mpt_tab <- function(m) mpt_trial %>% group_by(tool, type) %>% summarise(v = mr(.data[[m]]), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(type = factor(TYPE_LABEL[type], levels = TYPE_LABEL), method = factor(MX_TOOLS[tool], levels = MX_TOOLS)) %>%
  arrange(type) %>% select(method, type, v) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = v) %>% arrange(method)
kable(mpt_tab("sensitivity_stop"), caption = "Stop-level sensitivity by type")
kable(mpt_tab("sensitivity_exact"), caption = "Exact sensitivity by type")
details(mpt_tab("precision_stop"), "stop-level precision by type")
details(MPT %>% select(org, trial, tool, type, n_truth, n_pred, tp_stop, tp_exact, sensitivity_stop,
                       sensitivity_exact, precision_stop) %>%
          mutate(across(c(sensitivity_stop, sensitivity_exact, precision_stop), r3)) %>% arrange(org, tool, type, trial),
        "per organism, trial, tool and type")
MPTV <- function(tool, type, m) mpt_mean[[m]][mpt_mean$tool == tool & mpt_mean$type == type]
f3p <- function(x) if (length(x) == 0) "(pending)" else f3(x)
codan_mx <- MX_RAW %>% filter(tool == "codan") %>% distinct(org, trial)
```

On internal fragments TransDecoder has stop-level sensitivity `r f3(MPTV(TD, "internal", "sensitivity_stop"))`
and exact `r f3(MPTV(TD, "internal", "sensitivity_exact"))`. Prodigal has `r f3(MPTV("prodigal", "internal", "sensitivity_stop"))` /
`r f3(MPTV("prodigal", "internal", "sensitivity_exact"))`, GeneMarkS-T `r f3(MPTV("gmst", "internal", "sensitivity_stop"))` /
`r f3(MPTV("gmst", "internal", "sensitivity_exact"))` and CodAn `r f3p(MPTV("codan", "internal", "sensitivity_stop"))` /
`r f3p(MPTV("codan", "internal", "sensitivity_exact"))`
(CodAn: `r nrow(codan_mx)` of 21 runs scored so far; CodAn takes hours per input and its runs
were still going when this was knitted; its rows appear in the tables once `score_mixed.py` and
`02_partial_types.py` are re-run). The ATG-requiring classifiers (CPAT, CPC2, RNAsamba, Borf)
have stop-level sensitivity of at most `r f3(max(sapply(c("cpat", "cpc2", "rnasamba", "borf"), MPTV, type = "internal", m = "sensitivity_stop")))`
on internal fragments. The longest ORF of an internal fragment is almost always the reference frame, which has no stop
codon, so the baseline is near 1 on this type by construction (`r f3(MPTV("longest_orf", "internal", "sensitivity_exact"))`).

**5' partials by distance to the first in-frame ATG and by the share of the CDS removed**
(`five_prime_by_distance.tsv`, from `score_mixed.py`). On a 5' partial an exact match means the
prediction is left open at the fragment start. A stop-level match without an exact match usually
means the prediction starts at a downstream ATG. "none": no in-frame ATG in the remaining CDS.

```{r mixed-5p}
FD <- read_tab("benchmark", "final_v7", "five_prime_by_distance.tsv") %>%
  filter(!(org == "tthermophila" & tool %in% INCOMPATIBLE), tool %in% names(MX_TOOLS)) %>%
  mutate(trial = trial_of(variant))
fd_tab <- function(stratum_, m) {
  bins <- unique(FD$bin[FD$stratum == stratum_])
  FD %>% filter(stratum == stratum_) %>% group_by(tool, bin, trial) %>% summarise(v = median(.data[[m]]), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(tool, bin) %>% summarise(v = r3(mean(v)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(bin = factor(bin, levels = bins), method = factor(MX_TOOLS[tool], levels = MX_TOOLS)) %>% arrange(bin) %>%
    select(method, bin, v) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = bin, values_from = v) %>% arrange(method)
}
fd_n <- FD %>% filter(tool == TD) %>% group_by(stratum, bin, trial) %>% summarise(n = sum(n_truth), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(stratum, bin) %>% summarise(references = round(mean(n)), .groups = "drop")
kable(fd_tab("dist_first_inframe_atg", "sensitivity_exact"),
      caption = "5' partials: exact sensitivity (ORF left open) by nt from fragment start to first in-frame ATG")
kable(fd_tab("dist_first_inframe_atg", "sensitivity_stop"), caption = "5' partials: stop-level sensitivity by distance to first in-frame ATG")
kable(fd_tab("cut_frac", "sensitivity_exact"), caption = "5' partials: exact sensitivity by fraction of the CDS removed")
details(fd_n %>% filter(stratum == "dist_first_inframe_atg") %>% select(-stratum) %>%
          bind_rows(fd_n %>% filter(stratum == "cut_frac") %>% select(-stratum)),
        "references per bin (all organisms, mean over trials)")
details(FD %>% select(org, trial, tool, stratum, bin, n_truth, sensitivity_stop, sensitivity_exact) %>%
          arrange(org, tool, stratum, trial), "per organism, trial, tool and bin")
FDV <- function(tool, b) {
  d <- FD %>% filter(stratum == "dist_first_inframe_atg", tool == !!tool, bin == b) %>% group_by(trial) %>%
    summarise(v = median(sensitivity_exact), .groups = "drop")
  mean(d$v)
}
```

TransDecoder leaves `r f3(FDV(TD, "0-29"))` of the 5' partials open when an in-frame ATG lies within
30 nt of the fragment start, and `r f3(FDV(TD, "300+"))` when the first in-frame ATG is 300 nt or more
downstream. The corresponding values for Prodigal are `r f3(FDV("prodigal", "0-29"))` and
`r f3(FDV("prodigal", "300+"))`.

## Method rankings across inputs and measures

Each method is ranked in every combination of organism, stranded input (complete, complete with full
UTRs, fragments, complete + random, fragments + random) and measure (stop-level and exact sensitivity,
precision and F1): 7 organisms x 5 inputs x 6 measures = 210 categories. *T. thermophila* is left out,
because five of the eight methods do not support its genetic code (above); it is compared separately
under "Ciliate genetic code". Only the methods run on all
of these inputs are ranked: TransDecoder (release), Prodigal, GeneMarkS-T, CodAn, CPAT, CPC2, RNAsamba
and Borf (RNAsamba was not run on unstranded inputs; v6.0.0 and the longest-ORF baseline are not
ranked). Ties share the best rank. Because ranks ignore margins, the gap to the best method in each category
(best value minus the method's value) is reported too.

```{r rank-data}
RANK_TOOLS <- c(pytd_v7 = "TransDecoder", prodigal = "Prodigal", gmst = "GeneMarkS-T", codan = "CodAn",
                cpat = "CPAT", cpc2 = "CPC2", rnasamba = "RNAsamba", borf = "Borf")
RANK_INPUTS <- c(complete = "complete", complete_fullutr = "complete, full UTR", fragments = "fragments",
                 complete.wRand = "complete + random", fragments.wRand = "fragments + random")
RANK_MEASURES <- c(sensitivity_stop = "stop sensitivity", precision_stop = "stop precision",
                   f1_stop = "stop F1", sensitivity_exact = "exact sensitivity",
                   precision_exact = "exact precision", f1_exact = "exact F1")
rk <- S %>% filter(tool %in% names(RANK_TOOLS), variant %in% names(RANK_INPUTS)) %>%
  select(org, variant, tool, all_of(names(RANK_MEASURES))) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(RANK_MEASURES)), names_to = "measure", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(org, variant, measure) %>% filter(n_distinct(tool) == length(RANK_TOOLS), !any(is.na(value))) %>%
  mutate(rank = rank(-value, ties.method = "min"), gap = max(value) - value) %>% ungroup()
n_cat <- n_distinct(rk %>% select(org, variant, measure))
rank_summary <- function(d) d %>% group_by(tool) %>%
  summarise(categories = n(), first = sum(rank == 1), top3 = sum(rank <= 3), median_rank = median(rank),
            within_0.01 = mean(gap <= 0.01), within_0.03 = mean(gap <= 0.03), median_gap = median(gap),
            max_gap = max(gap)) %>%
  mutate(method = RANK_TOOLS[tool]) %>% arrange(desc(first + top3 / 100))
rs_all <- rank_summary(rk)
rs_measure <- rk %>% group_by(measure, tool) %>%
  summarise(first = sum(rank == 1), top3 = sum(rank <= 3), median_rank = median(rank), .groups = "drop")
td_rs <- rs_all %>% filter(tool == TD)
td_gap <- rk %>% filter(tool == TD) %>% group_by(measure) %>%
  summarise(median_gap = median(gap), max_gap = max(gap), first = sum(rank == 1), top3 = sum(rank <= 3))
td_worst <- rk %>% filter(tool == TD) %>% slice_max(gap, n = 1)
```

Categories ranked: `r n_cat`. TransDecoder ranks first in `r td_rs$first` (`r pct(td_rs$first / n_cat, 0)`)
and in the top three in `r td_rs$top3` (`r pct(td_rs$top3 / n_cat, 0)`), more than any other method; its
median rank is `r td_rs$median_rank`. It is within 0.01 of the best method in
`r pct(td_rs$within_0.01, 0)` of categories and within 0.03 in `r pct(td_rs$within_0.03, 0)`; its median gap
to the best is `r f3(td_rs$median_gap)` (next smallest: `r rs_all$method[order(rs_all$median_gap)][2]`,
`r f3(sort(rs_all$median_gap)[2])`). Its largest gap is `r f3(td_worst$gap)`
(`r ORG_LABEL[td_worst$org]`, `r RANK_INPUTS[td_worst$variant]`, `r RANK_MEASURES[td_worst$measure]`).
By measure, TransDecoder is never first in stop sensitivity (Prodigal is first in
`r rs_measure$first[rs_measure$measure == "sensitivity_stop" & rs_measure$tool == "prodigal"]` of 35) and
is first or tied first most often in stop F1
(`r td_gap$first[td_gap$measure == "f1_stop"]` of 35, median gap `r f3(td_gap$median_gap[td_gap$measure == "f1_stop"])`).

```{r rank-tables}
fmt_rs <- function(d) d %>% transmute(method, categories, first, `top 3` = top3, `median rank` = median_rank,
                                      `within 0.01` = pct(within_0.01, 0), `within 0.03` = pct(within_0.03, 0),
                                      `median gap` = f3(median_gap), `max gap` = f3(max_gap))
kable(fmt_rs(rs_all), caption = "Seven organisms (T. thermophila not ranked)")
kable(td_gap %>% transmute(measure = RANK_MEASURES[measure], first, `top 3` = top3,
                           `median gap` = f3(median_gap), `max gap` = f3(max_gap)),
      caption = "TransDecoder by measure (35 categories each)")
details(rs_measure %>% mutate(measure = RANK_MEASURES[measure], method = RANK_TOOLS[tool]) %>%
          select(measure, method, first, top3, median_rank) %>% arrange(measure, median_rank),
        "rank counts by measure and method")
details(rk %>% transmute(org = ORG_LABEL[org], input = RANK_INPUTS[variant], measure = RANK_MEASURES[measure],
                         method = RANK_TOOLS[tool], value = r3(value), rank, gap = r3(gap)) %>%
          arrange(org, input, measure, rank), "all ranks (one row per method and category)")
```

```{r figS4, fig.width = FULL_W, fig.height = 80 * MM}
tool_order <- rs_all$method
rank_bins <- rk %>% mutate(method = factor(RANK_TOOLS[tool], levels = rev(tool_order)),
                           bin = cut(rank, c(0, 1, 2, 3, 8), labels = c("1", "2", "3", "4-8"))) %>%
  count(method, bin)
pa <- ggplot(rank_bins, aes(n, method, fill = forcats::fct_rev(bin))) + geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`1` = "#08519c", `2` = "#4292c6", `3` = "#9ecae1", `4-8` = "#e5e5e5"),
                    breaks = c("1", "2", "3", "4-8"), name = "rank") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), breaks = c(0, 70, 140, 210)) +
  labs(x = sprintf("categories (of %d)", n_cat), y = NULL, title = "rank in each category")
heat_r <- rs_measure %>% mutate(method = factor(RANK_TOOLS[tool], levels = rev(tool_order)),
                                measure = factor(RANK_MEASURES[measure], levels = RANK_MEASURES))
pb <- ggplot(heat_r, aes(measure, method, fill = median_rank)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%d/%d", first, top3)), size = 1.55,
            colour = ifelse(heat_r$median_rank <= 3, "white", "#222222")) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#08519c", high = "#f0f0f0", limits = c(1, 8), name = "median rank") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "first / top 3 (of 35), by measure") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1), axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank())
pc <- ggplot(rk %>% mutate(method = factor(RANK_TOOLS[tool], levels = rev(tool_order))),
             aes(pmax(gap, 1e-4), method)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3, linewidth = 0.25, fill = "#deebf7") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1e-4, 1e-2, 1), labels = c("0", "0.01", "1")) +
  labs(x = "gap to best (log)", y = NULL, title = "gap to best")
figS4 <- (pa + pb + pc) + plot_layout(widths = c(0.9, 1.5, 0.8)) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title.position = "top", legend.key.width = unit(4, "mm"))
save_fig(figS4, "figS4_rankings", FULL_W, 70 * MM)
figS4
```

## Release versus earlier final defaults

The TransDecoder numbers the text quotes, computed from the earlier final defaults (`pytd_dev_v2`,
the runs the text and the current figure used) and from the release (`pytd_v7`).
